Volunteer divers bring a seagrass meadow back to life on the Portuguese coast

By Marta Sousa · 14 March 2025

A seagrass meadow that had all but vanished from the Sado estuary is growing back, thanks to a restoration project run by the Portuguese Institute for Ocean Restoration and hundreds of volunteer divers.

Since 2021, the volunteers have replanted 4,200 square metres of seabed with shoots of Zostera marina collected from healthy meadows further along the coast.

The project's marine biologist, Dr. Ana Ferreira, reported that 87% of the transplanted shoots survived their first winter, a rate far above what earlier restoration attempts in Europe had achieved.

Local fishermen have welcomed the recovery. The meadow shelters young cuttlefish and seahorses, and the regional fisheries office said that catches of cuttlefish in the estuary rose by 30% in 2024.

The institute now plans to train volunteers in three more coastal towns, hoping the same method can help restore seagrass along the Atlantic coast of Portugal.
